conviction_note: The only thing left standing is a small document-backed finding: the FY2025 20-F contingencies note shows the H2-2025 loss drivers were accrued in full (the $34.9M Coleman judgment plus fees, $6.93M of retroactive anti-dumping exposure) and the balance-sheet overhangs cleared in Q1 2026 (the NGCL guarantee settled 2026-01-09, about $28M of pledged deposits released Feb-Mar 2026). So H1 2026 is unlikely to carry a fresh charge of that size. That is +0.5. I emit +0.3 because the bar is unsourced (no analyst coverage, no company guide), the name's reaction history is two releases (+13.3% on H1 2025, about +2.5% on FY2025), and the stock has already run +15% in five days off its 52-week low.
bar: unsourced as a consensus: no analyst covers KNDI (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/kndi/, 'n/a ratings'), and the company gave no numeric 2026 guidance. As a proxy I use the prior-year H1 2025 revenue of $36.3M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1720250/000121390025078160/ea0253670-6k_kandi.htm). Every size is capped for that reason. The print_vs_bar read rests only on management's Q1 comment that the core business 'remained stable' and on Rawrr being consolidated since its December 2025 acquisition.
positioning_check: Finviz, read 2026-09-25: 1.26M shares short, 1.48% of float, days to cover 1.36 (settlement date not shown) (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=KNDI&ty=si). That is not a crowded short. There is no skew: the baseline chain is 'unusable_chain', with total OI 446 and a put/call OI ratio of 0.01, so the option market makes no directional statement. The 20-day average volume is about 81k shares, roughly $49k a day, which is below the $200k turnover floor.

findings.finding: The FY2025 20-F contingencies note (Note 22) says the H2-2025 loss drivers are already accrued: the Coleman/Champion judgment ($33.03M plus $1.85M in fees, under appeal since 2026-02-10 with a ruling expected in 12-18 months) and the critical-circumstances retroactive anti-dumping exposure ($6.93M plus interest). It also shows the NGCL loan guarantee fully settled on 2026-01-09 and about $28M of pledged deposits released in Feb-Mar 2026. So H1 2026 should not carry a repeat of the roughly $59M of H2-2025 charges (the $43.1M other loss plus $15.8M of impairments).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two confirmed releases only. The H1 2025 print, which showed net income of $1.7M on revenue down 39%, reacted +13.29% (baseline). The FY2025 print, carrying the $95.6M loss that includes these charges, rose about +2.5% after the call (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-kandi-technologies-sees-247-stock-rise-post-q4-2026-call-93CH-4641460). So this holder base has already looked through these charges once.
findings.source_date: 2026-04-28 (20-F for FY2025, filed alongside the FY2025 release https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/04/28/3282414/0/en/kandi-technologies-reports-full-year-2025-financial-results.html)
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody covers the name, and the note sits deep in the XBRL of a 20-F that the wire release does not reproduce: the release mentions 'anti-dumping duty expenses and increased litigation costs' with no amounts and nothing about accrual status. If the market had priced a clean H1, the stock would not be sitting at $49.6M of market cap against $211.9M of cash, restricted cash and CDs (about $113M net of short-term loans, notes payable and accrued liabilities). Most of that discount is plausibly the China-cash and governance discount, though, which this finding does not touch. Hence the small size.
findings.independence: Partial support from a different source: management said on the 2026-04-28 call that Q1 2026 core business 'remained stable', with better per-dealer sales (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/kandi-technologies-group-q4-earnings-152903704.html). That supports the absence of new deterioration, not the absence of charges.

outside_window.finding: Nasdaq minimum bid-price deficiency: the compliance period ends 2026-11-02 and the stock is at $0.60. A reverse split, or a transfer to the Capital Market for another 180 days, is likely. A reverse split in a microcap is usually sold, but the decision falls after the exit window unless it is announced with the results.

The appeal of the $33M Coleman judgment in the Texas 5th Court of Appeals was filed 2026-02-10, and the company expects a ruling in 12-18 months. A reversal would release an accrued liability of about $35M, roughly 70% of market cap.

searched_and_found_nothing: 2026 6-Ks: only three, the Nasdaq notice (05-08), a director appointment (06-04) and the Xinchu 51% acquisition for RMB20M (06-29). No buyback, divestment or financing (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001720250&type=6-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40)
Share buyback: the last programme was $30M in Nov 2023, and nothing has been announced in 2025-2026 (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/kandi-technologies-announces-share-buyback-130000141.html)
Insider filings: Form 3s on 2026-08-28 and 09-02 look like the new FPI Section 16 regime. No Form 4 buying or selling cluster found (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/KNDI/)

IEEPA tariff refund: SCOTUS struck the tariffs down 2026-02-20 and CBP's CAPE refunds are running, but Kandi has disclosed no refund claim or receivable, so there is no company-level number (https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/03/tariff-refund-mechanism-takes-shape)

EAPA golf-cart evasion cases 8247/8282/8286 (Apr-Aug 2026) name competitor importers (ICON, Denago, Bintelli, Atlas and others) but not Kandi/SC Autosports. Possible competitive relief, but it is only a macro-to-company hypothesis and was dropped (https://www.cbp.gov/document/publications/eapa-cons-case-8286-various-importers-notice-initiation-investigation-and)
Battery-swap revenue: the CATL/Qiji 18-station order and the Lin'an production start are both July 2026, after H1, so they do not land in the reported half (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/KNDI/)
Company IR site and Nasdaq short-interest page returned 503
baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The +15% five-day run-up off the 52-week low already carries some pre-print optimism, and my small positive does not cut against it, so the price plausibly holds most of what I found.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis): dropped the +0.5 finding that EAPA enforcement against competitor golf-cart importers helps Kandi's US sales. Neither the company nor a counterparty has said it, and ICON won an injunction against its interim measures.
Rule 6 (unsourced bar caps every size): cut the accrued-charges finding from +1.0 to +0.5.

Rule 3 (caveat reaches the number): the holder base looked through these same charges on the FY2025 print (+2.5%), and the stock is +15% in five days, so expected_move goes from +1.0 to +0.3, below the +0.5 sum.
History rebuild (baseline_history_trustworthy false): the base rate now uses two confirmed releases (+13.3% H1 2025, about +2.5% FY2025) instead of the baseline's single row.
Rule 8 left standing but not triggered: I have no confirmed unpriced company-level number to size up on the thin-coverage argument.
